newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-INDIA BEAT SOUTH AFRICA TO LIFT TITAN CUP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA BEAT SOUTH AFRICA TO LIFT TITAN CUP.

text.p: Leg-spinner Anil Kumble took four for 25 as India, improving with every match, beat favourites South Africa by 35 runs to win the Titan Cup in the triangular series final on Wednesday.

Chasing a modest Indian total of 220 for seven, the South Africans, who had won all six of their preliminary matches with ease, collapsed to 96 for seven and were finally all out for 185 in 47.2 overs.

Venkatesh Prasad made the early inroads by dismissing both Andrew Hudson and Lance Klusener for just seven each. Hudson scooped a catch to midwicket to allow Mohammed Azharuddin to join Australian Allan Border and West Indian Viv Richards as the only men to have taken 100 catches in one-day internationals.
The South Africans then rallied through Gary Kirsten (23) and Daryll Cullinan (30) before crumbling in the face of some testing bowling from Kumble.

The capacity crowd of 40,000 home supporters, noisily anticipating an Indian victory, were briefly silenced as off-spinner Pat Symcox (46) and wicketkeeper Dave Richardson (43) added 88 for the eighth wicket to keep South Africa's hopes alive.
But when Prasad and Kumble combined again to wrap up the innings, the celebrations began once more.

Earlier, home captain Sachin Tendulkar had top-scored with 67 in the Indian innings but, after the middle order had collapsed, it was a late burst of hitting by Ajay Jadeja which enabled them to reach a respectable 220 for seven in their 50 overs.
Jadeja, who struck a breezy 43 not out from 42 balls including two successive sixes off left-arm spinner Nicky Boje, added a vital 51 off 53 balls for the seventh wicket with Nayan Mongia.
Fanie de Villiers, who opened the South African attack, again bowled economically, conceding only four runs in his first four overs and ending with three for 32.

South African skipper Hansie Cronje singled out the bowling of Kumble and Prasad for special praise but was succint when asked what he thought was the turning point of the match: "The spin of the coin," he said.
